text_blocks.snippet: Losartan is a prescription medication used to treat high blood pressure, protect kidney function in people with type 2 diabetes, and reduce the risk of stroke. While generally well-tolerated, it can cause several common and serious side effects.
Most common side effects are mild and tend to improve over time as your body adjusts:

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly from a sitting or lying position)
Upper respiratory infections or a stuffy/runny nose
Digestive issues such as mild nausea, diarrhea, or stomach upset
Dry cough (much less common than with ACE inhibitors, but still possible)

text_blocks.snippet: Serious Side Effects (Require Prompt Medical Attention)
Contact your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience any of the following:

list.snippet: Severe allergic reaction (Angioedema): Sudden swelling of the face, lips, tongue, throat, eyes, hands, or feet, or difficulty breathing or swallowing.
High potassium levels (Hyperkalemia): Muscle weakness, slow, fast, or irregular heartbeat, or a feeling of numbness/tingling.
Kidney problems: A noticeable decrease in urination, or swelling in your ankles, feet, or hands.
Severe low blood pressure (Hypotension): Fainting, extreme lightheadedness, or blurry vision.
Liver issues: Yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice) or severe upper stomach pain.
Potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium, unless approved by your doctor, as losartan can raise potassium levels.
Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like ibuprofen or naproxen, which can worsen kidney function and reduce how well losartan works.
Pregnancy: Losartan should not be taken during pregnancy as it can cause injury or harm to an unborn baby.

text_blocks.snippet: For a detailed overview of precautions and usage guidelines, check the Mayo Clinic Losartan Guide or review the MedlinePlus Losartan Information.
